acceptance_criteria: Public, documented type `pub struct MetricThread { pub nominal: f64, pub pitch: f64 }` with methods `designation(&self) -> String` (e.g. `"M6"`, `"M2.5"`), `minor_diameter(&self) -> f64` (D − 1.082532·P, ISO 68-1) and `tap_drill_diameter(&self) -> f64` (D − P). The doc comments cite ISO 261 and ISO 68-1.

`pub const METRIC_COARSE: &[MetricThread]` holds, in ascending order, exactly: M2 0.4, M2.5 0.45, M3 0.5, M4 0.7, M5 0.8, M6 1.0, M8 1.25, M10 1.5, M12 1.75, M16 2.0, M20 2.5, M24 3.0 (nominal mm, pitch mm).
`pub fn metric_coarse(designation: &str) -> Result<MetricThread, KernelError>` looks up a size by designation (`"M6"`, also accepting lower case `"m6"` and surrounding whitespace).

Unit tests (no `occt`), values within 1e-4: `metric_coarse("M6")` has pitch 1.0, minor diameter 4.9175, tap drill 5.0. `metric_coarse("M3")`: pitch 0.5, minor 2.4587, tap drill 2.5. `metric_coarse("m10 ")`: pitch 1.5, minor 8.3762, tap drill 8.5. `metric_coarse("M2.5")` has pitch 0.45 and designation `"M2.5"`. The table has 12 rows, strictly ascending by nominal size, and every row's designation round-trips through `metric_coarse`.
Errors, each with a test and never a panic, all `InvalidInput`: an unknown size (`"M7"`), an empty string, a malformed string (`"6"`, `"Mx"`, `"M-6"`).
No new dependencies; no `unsafe`; `swx-kernel` still has no workspace dependencies.
`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` pass, and so do the CI `swx-kernel (occt)` job commands.
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
objective.description: M3-12b: Metric coarse thread table and tap-drill data (no OCCT)
